messages.subject: ponytail SPEC ready: fix audit as own step before review 3
messages.body: worker_status: partial (brainstorm merged at convergence 0.96; the invariant gate was cleared by the refactor plan, not by debate agreement): the mechanism is one fix audit per loop, run as its own Task T08a after the cycle-2 reviser and before review 3 (/sc:spec-panel-ponytail --fix-audit --re-review <R2> --baseline <v2>), in which a fresh session invokes ponytail:ponytail-review to write a per-fix table (claimed and validated severity, necessary, smaller alternative, keep/shrink/revert) and a stdlib script alone applies it (whole reverts only of hunks citing only minor ids, deletions only of fix-added words, never closing a finding review 2 graded blocking), and after review 3 the script computes the verdict, which can never turn a FAIL into a PASS. Predicted on the Arm B base: review-3 critical+major 3.3 (range 2.9 to 3.6, bar 3, about 35% chance of meeting it), growth after two cycles 27% (bar 44.4%), paired effect against a forked no-audit review 3 of about -0.2, with alternatives (a) after every cycle 3.2/26% and (b) triage before the first fix 3.5/26%; the measured attribution shows minor-fix reverts are worth only about 0.2 review-3 findings per run, so the lever is deleting surplus text of blocking fixes. Biggest risk: the auditor must spot, before review 3 does, the surplus words review 3 would attack (the assumed 35-50% capture is unmeasured), and a pure one-line name substitution cannot work because the S1 review-3 brief forbids any write but its report, so the experiment needs the inserted T08a Task; SPEC.md passed three fresh-context checks and the last blocking item found (a stale 23% share, now 27%) was fixed without a fourth check.
